slides.title: Four conditions decide whether the 2024 recovery holds
columns: What has to be true in 2024

points: Dry powder remains at a record after two slow deployment years
Funds raised in 2021 reach the end of their investment periods in 2024
Average cheque size returns to $60-80m from the $40m of 2023
Buyouts keep the share of deals they took in healthcare and manufacturing
Software and SaaS investment fell ~65% as sentiment hit business-model viability
Scale assets stayed funded, so sellers had no pressure to reprice
Secondary and continuation vehicles clear the 2021 vintage at a discount
Public comparables hold, so the private mark stops moving against the seller

cells.lead: Exits waited for the listing market
points: IPO windows opened only briefly, and strategics stayed on the sidelines
Hold periods extended past five years across the 2018-19 vintages
A listing window that stays open long enough to price a second cohort
Strategic buyers return with balance sheets rather than paper
Traditional sectors held ~75% of investments as investors backed proven models
Healthcare and advanced manufacturing grew while IT services reset
IT/ITeS deal value stabilises after a 65% decline
New-age tech clears its funding overhang rather than repricing again

note: Dry powder measured as uncalled capital in India-focused funds at year end
2023 figures are announced enterprise values and may not sum

slides.title: Financial institutions
slides.summary: Where the revenue pool sits, and what the credit institutions are doing with generative AI

slides.title: Retail and corporate banking hold two thirds of the revenue pool, mostly domestic

exhibit.heading: Banking revenue pool by business line and geography, 2025

annotations.text: Two thirds booked outside the home market

points: Retail is 70% domestic, so rate and deposit dynamics at home drive the largest pool
Markets is the most international, with two thirds of revenue booked in Europe and Asia
Payments is small but growing fastest, and skews to Asia
Wealth sits between the two: domestic clients, international assets

slides.title: In credit, governance rather than availability decides how far a generative-AI programme reaches

metrics.label: have access to external GenAI solutions
have no access to these tools

points: Access is broad but governed: 29 of 33 institutions have access and 52% gate it behind guideline training
Only 12 institutions open the tools to almost all colleagues; the rest keep them inside named teams
38% limit tools to specific areas rather than the whole workflow
The four without access cite regulatory uncertainty, not capability
Governance, not availability, is what decides how far a deployment reaches inside an institution

footnotes.text: Access granted to named teams rather than the whole institution

note: Shares are of the 33 institutions surveyed and do not sum

points.lead: Core regionals carry the most activity

with 6 of their 42 use cases fully deployed, the highest share of any pipeline here

points.lead: No institution has discontinued a use case
points.text: so far, though four in five remain before pilot and none of the 33 reports a retirement

points: Underwrite Indian private capital to 2018 levels, not 2019: a full recovery is a further 21% climb
Back the three sectors policy or demographics support - healthcare, manufacturing, energy - and wait on technology
